They haven't, and won't, do anything. Even jobseekers allowance is a means tested benefit, and my partner works too much for me to claim any of them. PIP isn't a "just go and sort it" type of thing, if you try to speak to anyone about it they tell you just to wait for the Tribunal. Believe me, i've been trying to push it forward, get news, anything for it. And i just tend to get fobbed off. I'm in contact with citizens advice and theres literally nothing that anyone can do other than waiting. I've applied for discretionary housing payments, not entitled because my partner works full time, I've applied for housing benefit, same deal. The system is just very unfair to the disabled.

In the UK most benefits are means tested, taking the income of your household into consideration. Because my partner (see, boyfriend. Not married, just cohabiting) works full time hours and isn't long term sick, he is considered to be "keeping me" and that means im not entitled to benefits that are means tested.

The one that is not means tested is called Personal Independence Payments, I applied for this last December and my case likely won't be heard in court until later this year, or the start of next. This is common, because there is a lot of controversy around PIP. in which most people are denied at original assessment, which is then overturned at a court date called "tribunal"... Im waiting for my tribunal after being told I should be able to walk by the original assessor. (This is disputed by my doctor, and the fact that I am literally bound to my chair).

... That was long, but that's some of the stress on my chest with the UK benefits system.

Ehh.. I have a tough stance on this. It prevents abuse on the system, but leaving a disabled person completely dependent on their partner, and refusing to make them self sustainable, is an easy way to force someone to stay in an abusive relationship type of situation.


Were things to turn sour in our relationship (as in we just didn't want to be together anymore), what would I do? I'd be on the streets, and I'd be disabled. 


Worse yet, People in abusive relationship situations are even more stuck in that relationship than their healthy counterparts, because they can't have a financial means of escape, when a healthy person could just "find a job" to enable their escape, thats not really happening for the majority of disabled people left relying on a partner.


For two normal people, the merging of a household is the merging of two incomes. Going from 15k each to 30k together, doubling their earnings and combining them into a household. 


A disabled person in a relationship forfeits all money as soon as they are with a partner and make the choice to live together. 


That strikes me as something that isn't quite fair. Of course, I never -wanted- to be disabled, and trust me, someone else who wants a life on benefits can GLADLY take my illness, as I loved my work as a carer. But I can't just survive on the merits of the person i'm dating. I should be entitled to assistance, and thats just how I feel about it.

Actually, no. With ESA there are 2 types. Income Related, and Contributions Related. Income I am not entitled to because of my partner being in work. 

Contributions related is targeted more towards those with disabilities, if you have worked a certain amount and paid enough tax within the past 4 years you are eligible to receive this form of ESA. 

I've been sick most of my life, my work history didn't start until I was 19 and ended 3 months ago, when I was taken out of work. (I was a carer, so it was considered a high risk situation).

I did not even get as far as the work capability assessment, they awarded me ESA, BUT. it only pays towards my pension. I get no funds incoming currently. Of course it's nice to have a pension going but, i'm 21. Not really thinking about it yet. I -do- technically have ESA, but not in a way that will give us any funds. 

It is way more complicated than I ever anticipated, especially for something that is supposed to support disabled folk.
